abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a unified information-theoretic framework for visual scene representation learning that fundamentally reconceptualizes how semantic coherence and spatial context interact in computer vision systems. Current approaches to scene interpretation typically rely on task-specific architectures with limited theoretical grounding, creating fragmented understanding across recognition, segmentation, and 3D vision domains. We propose modeling visual scene representations through the lens of information bottlenecks and mutual information optimization, where meaningful visual features emerge from maximizing relevant information while minimizing redundant encoding. Our theoretical analysis reveals that scene interpretation can be systematically decomposed into hierarchical information flows between object entities, spatial layouts, and semantic categories, enabling principled reasoning about visual relationships. The framework provides rigorous bounds on representation quality and establishes connections to neurobiological models of visual perception. Experiments across scene classification, object recognition, and semantic segmentation demonstrate that the proposed information-theoretic paradigm achieves superior generalization compared to contrastive and reconstruction-based alternatives. This work contributes a foundational theoretical model that unifies disparate visual understanding tasks under a common mathematical framework, opening new directions for visual learning research.

We present a theoretical analysis revealing the implicit optimization dynamics underlying modern visual recognition networks and demonstrate how this understanding leads to significant improvements in deep learning for vision. Prior research on neural architecture design has largely relied on empirical observations without rigorous theoretical foundations, limiting systematic improvement of visual learning systems. Our analysis shows that standard gradient-based training of convolutional networks implicitly minimizes an information-theoretic objective closely related to the PAC-Bayes generalization bounds, providing a principled connection between network optimization and statistical learning theory. Based on this theoretical insight, we derive novel regularization terms that directly constrain the information-theoretic quantities governing generalization performance. The proposed training framework introduces a principled approach to balancing representation compactness against discriminative power, addressing the trade-off between fitting training data and maintaining generalization ability. Extensive experiments on standard object recognition and image segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that the derived regularization approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in limited-data regimes where theoretical guarantees become critical. This work bridges the gap between practical deep learning optimization and theoretical generalization analysis, providing both insight and effective algorithmic improvements for computer vision applications.

We introduce a novel end-to-end framework for integrated 3D scene understanding that fundamentally rethinks the traditional pipeline architecture for robotic vision applications. Conventional approaches to 3D vision typically employ sequential processing stages for depth estimation, semantic segmentation, and geometric reconstruction, leading to accumulated errors and inefficient computation unsuitable for real-time robotics. Our proposed system unifies depth estimation, semantic scene interpretation, and 3D reconstruction within a single differentiable architecture, enabling joint optimization of all components for maximum synergy. The framework introduces cross-modal attention mechanisms that facilitate information flow between geometric and semantic representations, allowing learned features to simultaneously encode 3D structure and object identity. The architectural design emphasizes computational efficiency and memory conservation, achieving real-time performance on embedded platforms suitable for autonomous navigation. Extensive evaluation on indoor and outdoor scenes demonstrates that the unified approach significantly outperforms staged pipelines in both accuracy and speed, particularly for complex environments with severe occlusion and varying illumination. This paradigm shift from modular to integrated scene understanding represents a fundamental advance in vision applications for robotics, enabling more robust and responsive visual systems for real-world deployment.

This paper presents a significantly enhanced object recognition system that addresses critical limitations in handling occlusion and scale variation through innovative architectural design and training strategies. Existing state-of-the-art detectors struggle with partially occluded objects and dramatic scale changes common in real-world visual scenarios, limiting practical deployment in autonomous systems. We introduce a multi-scale feature fusion mechanism with hierarchical attention that explicitly models occlusion patterns and scale-aware representations within a unified detection framework. The proposed architecture incorporates novel attention gates that dynamically weight feature contributions based on visibility and scale relevance, enabling robust recognition even when objects are severely truncated. We also develop an improved anchor assignment strategy that better handles extreme scale variations through adaptive matching criteria. Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements in mean average precision, with particularly significant gains on heavily occluded objects and small-scale targets. The system maintains competitive inference speed through efficient feature sharing and optimized attention computation, making it suitable for real-time vision applications. This work provides a practical solution for robust object recognition in adverse conditions, advancing the state of the art in pattern recognition for challenging operational environments.
